problem: Which expression represents one possible solution to 25k^2/sqrt(25k^2+x^2) = 65 - x^2/sqrt(25k^2+x^2), where k is a positive constant?
notes: Exact equation and choices from the user-supplied screenshot of a hard SAT problem. The two fractions have the same denominator, so their sum is sqrt(25k^2+x^2)=65, giving x^2=65^2-25k^2 and the positive branch sqrt(65^2-25k^2), choice B. A real solution also requires 0<k<=13; SAT asks for one possible expression under the values of k for which a real solution exists. A clear solution must explain the common-denominator cancellation rather than hide it.
